query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adjusting the HVAF-i7 parameters to increase particle velocity—specifically by adopting an optimal spray distance of 300–350 mm as demonstrated in MCrAlY coatings via the M3 system—will enhance deposition efficiency and allow for the attainment of a thicker, adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with 15–45 μm particle size, as used in prior HVAF-M3 studies.
generation.intervention: Increase the particle velocity of the feedstock by adjusting the HVAF-i7 spray parameters with a nozzle-spray distance in the 300–350 mm range.
generation.conditions: Deposition using an HVAF-i7 torch under similar as-sprayed conditions but with high particle velocity resulting from the optimized nozzle distance; service conditions include high-temperature thermal-barrier applications in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced kinetic energy of particles during flight leading to improved flattening and bonding upon impact.
generation.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases the kinetic energy of the particles, promoting more complete substrate impingement, reduced rebound, and improved inter-particle bonding. This leads to a higher deposition efficiency and thicker coating while maintaining low oxidation levels during deposition.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant increase in the deposited bond coat thickness relative to the baseline 15–45 μm feedstock application in the HVAF-i7 process, while preserving coating adhesion and integrity as well as minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.baseline: Coating produced with 15–45 μm feedstock using standard HVAF-i7 conditions that yields acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: The intervention remains effective provided that the increased particle velocity does not induce excessive in-flight oxidation or substrate damage; it is effective on substrates within small-diameter geometries (down to 120 mm) and under high-temperature service conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements in deposition efficiency and coating thickness are uncertain, and potential trade-offs such as increased oxidation or thermal stresses at the substrate require further verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a side-by-side comparative study using the HVAF-i7 torch. One set uses standard spray parameters with the 15–45 μm feedstock, and the other set is processed with modified parameters to increase particle velocity by setting the nozzle-spray distance to 300–350 mm. All other processing conditions remain constant. Evaluate the thickness, adhesion, and oxidation levels of the bond coats.
measurements: Adhesion strength using standardized bond strength tests
Oxidation levels assessed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings produced with the increased particle velocity do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in thickness or if they show worsening adhesion/oxidation relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis that increasing particle velocity enhances deposition efficiency for thicker coatings is falsified.

chosen.approach: Optimize HVAF spray parameters via higher particle velocity and 300–350 mm distance
